summary: This is a Docker Compose configuration that defines a single service called 'app'. It builds a Docker image from the Dockerfile in the current directory, passing in customizable build arguments for the app directory, Python version, and timezone with sensible defaults. The service then runs as a container with specific security settings, port mapping, and environment configuration.

explanations.9: This passes the APP_HOME variable to the Docker build process; if APP_HOME isn't set in your environment, it defaults to /app using the ${VAR:-default} syntax.
explanations.10: Same pattern as line 9—it lets you override the Python version when building, but uses Python 3.13 if you don't specify one.
explanations.11: Sets the timezone for the container; defaults to Europe/Brussels if TIMEZONE isn't provided.
explanations.14: The container will load environment variables from a .env file in your project root instead of defining them inline here.
explanations.16: Maps port 8000 from inside the container to port 8000 on your machine; the %% syntax suggests this might be replaced by a templating tool later.
explanations.17: Runs the container as user ID 1001 with group ID 1001 instead of root, which is a security best practice.
explanations.19: Prevents the container from gaining new privileges, even if a process inside tries to escalate permissions—another security hardening measure.
